title: Light Frame Raises $5.1 Million to Modernise Private Banking Technology
summary:
Light Frame, the financial technology company providing modern core banking and portfolio management software for the wealth industry, today announced the successful closing of an oversubscribed $5.1 million Seed financing round.
The round was led by Fortino Ventures, with participation from Sidekick Partners, Tenity, Chamaeleon, and AltaIR Capital, alongside existing investors including Rogue Venture Partners, New Stack Ventures, and Studio Alpha.
The financing comes amid growing institutional adoption of Light Frame's technology across EMEA, where the company is supporting live client operations and expanding its presence in the private banking and wealth management markets.
Revolutionizing the wealth industry
Across the wealth industry, institutions continue to rely on technology built on architectures developed decades ago.  The result is an industry constrained by infrastructure that is too slow to implement, too costly to operate, and not capable enough to meet the industry’s evolving needs.
Light Frame has developed a new generation of core banking and portfolio management technology designed specifically for the wealth industry. Engineered in Switzerland, the platform combines comprehensive banking and investment capabilities with a cloud-native, API-first architecture designed around artificial intelligence. Through embedded AI capabilities and its secure interoperability layer, the platform enables institutions to automate complex operations, improve employee productivity and deliver more sophisticated client services. Its fully modular design allows institutions to modernise individual components of their existing infrastructure or adopt a complete solution, significantly reducing implementation timelines, operational complexity and total cost of ownership.
 “Light Frame delivers foundational technology with the sophistication institutions require,” said Schuyler Weiss, Co-founder and CEO of Light Frame. “AI is redefining what technology can deliver, but the realization of its potential in the Wealth industry is dependent on the underlying infrastructure. The architecture must be designed around this future, without compromising the security, resilience and trust fundamental to banking. In Fortino and our broader investor group, we have found partners who share our ambition to build that foundation for the next generation of wealth management.”
Light Frame was founded in 2024 by Schuyler Weiss, founder and former CEO of Alpian, Switzerland's first cloud-native private bank; Mathieu Clément, Alpian's former COO and CIO; and technologists Philippe Kernevez and Gregory Bataille. The founding team brings direct experience building and operating a regulated Swiss bank, including the challenges associated with implementing and maintaining traditional banking infrastructure.
"We are excited to back a team that is exceptionally credible in this space,” said Hugh Phelan, Investment Manager at Fortino Ventures “Schuyler and the team have run a regulated Swiss bank on the kind of infrastructure they are now replacing. Few founders in wealth technology have lived the problem this closely, and fewer still have the technical depth to solve it. For a bank, moving sensitive data and live operations onto a new platform is an act of trust, and this team has earned the right to ask for it."
The funding will support continued investment in the platform, expansion of implementation and client delivery capacity, and the growth of Light Frame's commercial activities, initially focused on EMEA.

content: Fintech startup Light Frame has successfully closed an oversubscribed $5.1 million Seed financing round led by Fortino Ventures. The company provides modern core banking and portfolio management software designed to help private banking and wealth management institutions replace outdated legacy infrastructure. The new capital will be used to expand platform development, client delivery capacity, and commercial activities across the EMEA region.

OpenPayd Hits $107 Million Annual Recurring Revenue as Fiat and Stablecoin Business Expands
summary:
OpenPayd, a leading provider of financial infrastructure, reached an annual recurring revenue of $107 million in October, following 44% year-on-year revenue growth to $25.4 million in the second quarter of its FY27 financial year. The results reflect continued demand across its fiat and stablecoin infrastructure.
The results reflect continued expansion across OpenPayd’s established fiat infrastructure alongside a growing contribution from stablecoin orchestration. Fiat infrastructure accounted for 70% of first-half revenue growth, with stablecoin orchestration contributing the remaining 30%.
 
OpenPayd launched its stablecoin infrastructure in May 2025, extending its platform across blockchain rails and enabling businesses to move between fiat and digital assets through a single infrastructure layer. First-half revenue from stablecoin orchestration increased from $0.5 million to $3.9 million year-on-year, as the infrastructure entered its second year of operation.
 

Iana Dimitrova, Chief Executive Officer at OpenPayd, said: “Passing $100 million in annual recurring revenue is an important milestone for OpenPayd. What’s particularly significant is where that growth is coming from – continued expansion across our fiat business, alongside a meaningful contribution from stablecoin orchestration.
 
“Our clients don’t need to make a bet on which rail will win. They need interoperable infrastructure that allows them to move and manage money across both, and use what works best for each flow. These results show how that approach is translating into growth, as existing clients do more with OpenPayd and new clients come onto the platform.”
 
Customers onboarded during FY27 contributed 34% of first-half banking and payments revenue growth. Stablecoin orchestration accounted for 32% of revenue from those new customers, reflecting its role in attracting new business as well as supporting existing clients.
 
As of October 2026, OpenPayd served more than 1,260 corporate clients and processed more than $360 billion in annualised transaction volume. Client balances held exceeded $1 billion, reflecting the scale of activity supported across the platform.

The platform now serves over 1,260 corporate clients and processes over $360 billion in transaction volume.

Avaloq launches Avaloq Mosaic, a modular platform for wealth managers
summary:
Avaloq, a global wealth technology firm and part of NEC Corporation, today announced its entry into the U.S. market with the launch of Avaloq Mosaic, a modular platform for wealth managers seeking to modernize investment technology without requiring a full platform replacement.
Avaloq Mosaic connects investment data and portfolio processes across existing systems, helping firms introduce new capabilities progressively. Many U.S. wealth managers rely on complex technology environments built up over years of growth and acquisitions. This can make it harder to support personalized investment strategies at scale, respond rapidly to market developments and adopt AI-enabled operating models.
Avaloq Mosaic debuts in the U.S. with two core capabilities, Portfolio IQ and Allocator. Portfolio IQ provides a real-time investment view, consolidating holdings, transactions and portfolio information across multiple accounts, custodians and other sources. Allocator translates investment strategies into portfolios across large and complex client books, supporting portfolio construction, personalization and ongoing management at scale.
Together, Portfolio IQ and Allocator provide a connected foundation for investment data and portfolio management. The broader Avaloq Mosaic offering also includes Agent Connect, which provides firms’ AI tools with governed access to verified investment data. Avaloq will expand the offering with additional capabilities, including Tax for tax-aware investment management, Asset Servicing for position keeping and securities-event administration, and Lending for margin and securities-backed lending decisions.
Built for complex wealth environments, Avaloq Mosaic combines a composable, cloud-native and API-first architecture with the governance and operating discipline required by large financial institutions.
Martin Greweldinger, Group CEO of Avaloq, said: “The U.S. is the world’s largest and one of the most sophisticated wealth markets, with distinct demands on the technology supporting advisors and clients. For more than four decades, Avaloq has built and operated technology for wealth managers across major global markets. With Avaloq Mosaic, we are bringing that experience to the U.S., giving firms the flexibility to modernize their technology, make better use of their investment data and introduce new capabilities without replacing the systems they already rely on.”
Suzzanna Gill, President, Avaloq U.S., said: “U.S. wealth managers are balancing greater scale with increasingly sophisticated portfolios and rising client demand for faster, more personalized insight, often on technology infrastructures built over many years. The opportunity for firms is to connect investment data with processes they already have, so they can modernize where it creates the greatest business impact.”
Avaloq has established a U.S. leadership team with experience across wealth management, brokerage, advisory technology and business transformation. Gill has extensive experience in wealth management transformation and building technology-enabled businesses in the U.S. Joel Lewis, Managing Director, U.S. Region, brings experience spanning self-directed brokerage, scaled advisory and full-service wealth management, with a focus on product strategy, transformation and business development.
Avaloq supports more than 170 financial institutions globally and reinvests 20% of its software revenue in research and development. Its technology helps wealth managers and private banks automate processes, streamline operations and manage complexity at scale.
